overview.text: The recording shows a strategy game with a world or territory map, a detailed city view, resource counters, land-claim controls, and a Heroes & Army roster panel.

core_loop.text: The visible activities include switching between a regional map and city view, inspecting a land parcel or claim panel, and opening hero and army management screens.
The footage suggests a strategy-management loop that links territory expansion, city development, resource management, and hero-led armies; the operational dependencies are not demonstrated.

controls.text: The interface exposes clickable-looking map controls, city navigation tabs, a land panel with action buttons, and tabs in the hero roster.
The input method and whether actions resolve immediately or over time are not shown.

rules.text: Several resource totals are displayed across the top bar. A land information panel includes a claim action and a visible cost or requirement area.
The video does not clearly show a completed claim, a resource deduction, combat resolution, or a territory ownership change that can be confidently attributed to a specific input.
The army roster names three heroes together under a formation or oath heading; the tactical consequences of that selection are not shown.

progression.text: The camera alternates between an isometric regional map and a detailed, animated city overview.
The hero management window shows a named three-hero group and a larger hero roster with portraits.
A farm or land-related panel appears over the city view at the end of the recording.

ui_feedback.text: The top bar presents multiple resource counters; side panels provide land information or army details; navigation tabs span the bottom of the city view.
The hero window groups selected heroes separately from the broader roster and offers multiple tabs, implying distinct roster or army-management views.

art.text: The world map uses a clear isometric view with small terrain objects and parcel markers, while the city view switches to a detailed, warm-toned settlement with roads, buildings, fields, and moving people.
The camera transitions between strategic overview and city-level presentation rather than following an individual character.

audio.text: Audio is present in the source file, but no sound-specific claim is included because the analysis focused on the visible evidence frames.

remake.text: Build a 2D or isometric map with selectable land parcels, a small resource bar, and one city that opens from the map.
Add one land detail panel and make claim costs update resources and parcel ownership visibly.
Add a hero roster with a three-slot army, then connect the selected roster to a simple encounter only after map and city interactions are clear.
For a first prototype, a data-driven UI in Godot, Unity, or a web-based strategy shell can validate the management loop; choose the presentation technology after testing the desired city scene.

unknowns.text: What actions consume each displayed resource, and how do resources regenerate?
What are the exact requirements and effects of claiming land?
How do heroes affect armies, battles, and city management?
Is there an active combat or battle-resolution system in the recorded build?
What are the long-term victory, defeat, and progression conditions?
